headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: n8n can read/write shared files and execute commands, while cognee handles personal/finance/support data and can be fed into workflows without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is plausible because n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate workflow nodes, while cognee processes documents and support data. If n8n ingests cognee-produced text from shared files or workflow outputs, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. No explicit shared channel is documented, so this is inferred.
conditions: IF n8n reads cognee output from a shared file or workflow node without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF cognee content is passed into n8n prompts or node parameters as trusted text, instructions can be hijacked.
mitigations: Add a strict content-to-instruction separator in the workflow.
Require allowlisted templates for any text passed from cognee to n8n.
Insert a manual review step before n8n executes actions from cognee output.
Use separate directories for raw cognee output and executable workflow inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening across the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while n8n has broad network egress and can access the server filesystem plus many integration nodes. In default workflow automation, sensitive data can flow from cognee into n8n and then out to third-party services. The blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach.
conditions: IF cognee outputs personal or finance data into an n8n workflow, that data can be transmitted onward.
IF an n8n integration node sends workflow contents to an external API, sensitive fields may leave the environment.
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows to non-sensitive test data.
Disable or remove outbound integration nodes for sensitive workflows.
Add field-level redaction before any n8n handoff.
Store cognee outputs in a segregated directory with access controls.
requires-engineering: implement DLP or policy-based egress filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to shared mutable resources: cognee has session memory and n8n can write the filesystem and execute shell commands. n8n also supports multiple instances with shared state via datastore and connected systems. Without locking, concurrent writes can corrupt workflow state or overwrite artifacts. The interaction is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore, race conditions can occur.
IF n8n Execute Command modifies files while cognee updates session memory artifacts, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate write directories per agent.
Serialize writes through a single queue or lock file.
Disable concurrent runs for shared workflows.
Use immutable output filenames with timestamps.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestration agent that can act on workflow outputs, while cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If n8n treats cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions such as API calls or file changes. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so unsafe automation is plausible by default.
conditions: IF n8n uses cognee output as a trigger or parameter source without validation, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF cognee emits incorrect decisions or workflow patterns, n8n can propagate them into integrations.
mitigations: Add a validation step before any n8n action node.
Require human approval for high-impact workflow branches.
Limit cognee output to suggestions, not commands.
Log and diff all generated parameters before execution.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly handles personal data and finance data, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, residency, and subject-rights handling if regulated data is routed through n8n. The profiles do not prove a specific residency violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is routed through n8n workflows, retention and logging policies must align.
IF n8n stores workflow logs containing personal data longer than cognee's policy, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in n8n workflows.
Review retention settings and purge schedules.
Mask sensitive fields in logs and execution history.
Separate credentials from data-processing workflows.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a data-processing agreement and residency controls.
